fullPassage: Living things are not confined to the familiar temperate realm of land, water, and sunlight inhabited by plants and plant-eating animals. They can be found in the darkest depths of the ocean, in hot volcanic mud, in pools beneath the frozen surface of the Antarctic, and buried kilometers deep in the Earth's crust. The creatures that live in these extreme environments are generally unfamiliar, not only because they are inaccessible, but also because they are mostly microscopic. In more homely habitats, too, most organisms are too small for us to see without special equipment: they tend to go unnoticed, unless they cause a disease or rot the timbers of our houses. Studies of bacteria have helped us become familiar with those species of industrial importance, such as those used in breaking down waste materials. Yet microorganisms make up most of the total mass of living matter on our planet. Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and specifically through the analysis of DNA sequences, have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth that is not grossly distorted by our biased perspective as large animals living on dry land.

④ influenced(영향 받은) — 다른 의미
det.tip: biased ↔ impartial/objective. 편향된 ↔ 공정한/중립적.

questions.passage:
(A) Yet microorganisms make up most of the total mass of living <u>matter</u> on our planet.
(B) No matter how hard you try, some problems just cannot be solved overnight.
questions.stem:
다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 'matter'의 의미가 서로 같으면 S, 다르면 D를 고르시오.
(A) Yet microorganisms make up most of the total mass of living <u>matter</u> on our planet.
(B) No matter how hard you try, some problems just cannot be solved overnight.

det.korean: (A) living matter = 살아있는 물질. (B) No matter how = '아무리 ~해도'. 의미 다름.
det.analysis:
① S, 둘 다 '물질' — (B)는 물질 아님
② S, 둘 다 '문제' — (A)는 문제 아님
③ D, (A)='문제' — (A) matter = 물질이지 문제가 아님
④ D ←정답 — (A) matter = 물질(substance). (B) No matter how = 아무리 ~해도(관용 표현)
det.tip: matter: ①물질(substance) ②문제(issue) ③중요하다(verb). No matter how = 양보 관용구.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "relating to molecules; involving the analysis of very small particles that make up substances"

det.korean: '분자에 관한; 물질을 구성하는 매우 작은 입자의 분석을 수반하는' = molecular(분자의).
det.analysis:
① microscopic(현미경의) — 매우 작은이지 분자 관련이 아님
② industrial(산업적) — 다른 의미
③ molecular ←정답 — 분자(molecule)에 관한. DNA 분자 분석에 사용
④ temperate(온화한) — 기후 관련, 다른 의미
det.tip: molecular = relating to molecules. 'molecular analysis' = 분자 분석.

questions.passage: Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and specifically through the analysis of DNA __________ (sequence), have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth that is not grossly distorted by our biased perspective.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)
Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and specifically through the analysis of DNA __________ (sequence), have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth.

det.korean: DNA __________ (sequence) → sequences(복수). 'analysis of DNA sequences' 에서 sequence의 복수형.
det.analysis: 'the analysis of DNA sequences' — DNA 서열들(복수). sequence(단수) → sequences(복수).
det.tip: sequence(단수) → sequences(복수). analysis of DNA sequences = DNA 서열 분석.

questions.passage: Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and __________ (specific) through the analysis of DNA sequences, have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth that is not grossly distorted by our biased perspective as large animals living on dry land.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)
Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and __________ (specific) through the analysis of DNA sequences, have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth.

det.korean: specifically = 특히, 구체적으로. specific(형용사) → specifically(부사). 동사 'through'를 수식하는 부사 형태.
det.analysis: 'and specifically through the analysis' — through를 수식하는 부사. specific(형용사) → specifically(부사, -ally 추가).
det.tip: specific(형용사) → specifically(부사). and ___ through = 특히 ~을 통해.

questions.passage: Living things are not confined to the familiar temperate realm of land, water, and sunlight inhabited by plants and plant-eating animals. They can be found in the darkest depths of the ocean, in hot volcanic mud, in pools beneath the frozen surface of the Antarctic, and buried kilometers deep in the Earth's crust. The creatures that live in these extreme environments are generally unfamiliar, not only because they are inaccessible, but also because they are mostly microscopic. In more homely habitats, too, most organisms are too small for us to see without special equipment: they tend to go unnoticed, unless they cause a disease or rot the timbers of our houses. Studies of bacteria have helped us become familiar with those species of industrial importance, such as those used in breaking down waste materials. Yet microorganisms __________ most of the total mass of living matter on our planet. Only recently, through new methods of molecular analysis and specifically through the analysis of DNA sequences, have we begun to get a picture of life on Earth that is not grossly distorted by our biased perspective as large animals living on dry land.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미생물이 지구 살아있는 물질의 대부분을 '구성한다(make up)' = 이루고 있다.
det.analysis:
① break down(분해하다) — 폐기물 분해는 앞 문장. 여기는 '구성'이 맞음
② give up(포기하다) — 의미 부적절
③ look for(찾다) — 의미 부적절
④ make up ←정답 — 'microorganisms make up most of the total mass'. 구성하다
det.tip: make up = constitute(구성하다). 미생물이 총 생물량의 대부분을 이룸.
